title: Chat-format SFT export with a token budget
scenario: Convert raw support-chat turns into system/user/assistant SFT examples: map and merge roles, trim to user-first/assistant-last, drop the oldest exchange until the example fits max_tokens, and hold back excluded tags.

verified.why_correct: `str.split()` with no argument splits on any whitespace run and returns [] for an empty string, so it counts words exactly as rule 5 says. It looks like a cousin of the tag-splitting code, but only `split(";")` produces empty entries.

bugs.title: Blank tag cells produce an empty tag
bugs.old: return [t.strip().lower() for t in clean(raw).split(";") if t.strip()]
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_example_tags: c02 and c09 have tags [""] instead of ["general"], and c08 has an extra "". Test 2 test_tag_counts: an empty-string key with count 3 appears and general is missing.
bugs.why: `"".split(";")` is `[""]`, not `[]`. A blank cell becomes a one-element list holding an empty tag, which is truthy, so the `general` default never applies; the trailing `;` on c08 adds an empty tag too.
hints: Where does the empty-string key in tag_counts come from?
Look at what parse_tags returns for a blank cell and for `coding;billing ;`.
Filter out empty entries: `... for t in clean(raw).split(";") if t.strip()`.
probes: Why is count_tokens' `.split()` safe while this `.split(";")` is not?

bugs.title: Budget loop config reads the generation limit
bugs.symptom: Test 1: c07 shows up as an example, c03 has 86 tokens and c10 73 (no truncation, dropped_messages 0). Test 2: c07 is missing from rejected, examples is 8, coding counts 2 and total_tokens is 417 instead of 295.
bugs.why: The export budget is taken from `max_new_tokens` (256) instead of `max_tokens` (60). Nothing exceeds 256, so c03 and c10 are never truncated and c07 is accepted instead of rejected as too_long.
bugs.unblocks: The token, truncation and rejection tests, and it exposes B3.
hints: c03 has 86 tokens with a 60-token budget, yet nothing was dropped. What budget is the code using?
Look at how load_config builds the settings dict, and compare with config.json.
probes: Why was the truncation loop impossible to test while this was wrong?
How would you make a config mix-up like this fail loudly?

bugs.why: Slicing off one message at a time leaves an example that can start with an assistant turn (c10 starts with "Yes, and no fees."), and `dropped` still grows by 2 per step, so c03 reports 4 dropped messages.

Why was this invisible until the budget came from the right config key?

context_qa.q: What is the flow inside build_dataset()?
context_qa.a: It loads the config, the conversation index (conv id → tags) and the grouped turns. For each conversation in index order it applies the `general` default, checks excluded tags, builds the body with `chat.to_messages`, runs `budget.fit_to_budget` with the system message, and stores the example or a rejection reason. The summary is computed from those two dicts at the end.

context_qa.q: What does to_messages do with roles it doesn't know?
context_qa.a: It looks each role up in `ROLE_MAP`; a role missing from the map (such as `system` or `tool`) gives None and the turn is skipped, as is a turn with empty text. Consecutive same-role messages are merged with a newline.

Either None (rejected as too long) or a tuple `(body, dropped)`, where `body` is the remaining non-system messages and `dropped` is a counter increased inside the loop. It loops while `count_tokens([system] + body)` exceeds `max_tokens`.

context_qa.q: Which config keys does load_config read?
context_qa.a: It returns a dict with `system_prompt` (stripped), `max_tokens` (as int) and `exclude_tags` (a set of trimmed, lower-cased strings). Other keys in config.json are not returned.

context_qa.q: How are turns ordered inside a conversation?
context_qa.a: `load_turns` groups rows by lower-cased conv id and sorts each group by the integer `turn` value, so file order does not matter.
A Counter over every tag of every accepted example (rejected conversations are not counted), returned as a dict sorted by tag.
